holdings.description: A complete individual of ellipsoidal form, which had been used as a pounder by the natives.

metbull.alternateNameNote: MetBull lists Xiquipilco as a synonym of Toluca. Both source occurrences describe the old Toluca Valley Mexican iron and agree with that identity.

holdings.description: A complete individual, the surface of which has scaled off somewhat. A polished and etched surface shows coarse Widmanstätten figures.

metbull.alternateNameNote: MetBull lists Tejupilco as a Toluca synonym; the source reports 1784 while MetBull reports 1776.

holdings.description: A rectangular chiseled and sawed fragment. Shows poor Widmanstätten figures.
A sawed, cuneiform piece showing part of an original surface pit.
A sawed slab showing natural surface on one edge. Etched surface shows small, indistinct markings.
A complete individual, irregularly meniscus-shaped. Surface pitted and torn. Etched surface shows Widmanstätten figures.
A slab 180 x 123 x 5 to 9 mm. in size. Both sides have been etched and show the typical Widmanstätten figures very perfectly. Three edges show the original surface of the mass.

metbull.alternateNameNote: MetBull treats abbreviated forms such as Mt. as implicit synonyms. The 1884 Santa Fe County pallasite context matches official Glorieta Mountain.

holdings.description: A polished slab 80 x 75 x 6 mm., one surface etched, showing excellent Widmanstätten figures.

A polished slab 278 x 137 x 7 to 17 mm. in size, an entire section of the mass. Much cohenite is present, frequently inclosing flakes and plates of schreibersite. Three irregularly ellipsoidal nodules are prominent in the mass. They consist of troilite associated with more or less of a relatively soft graphitic (?) substance, and surrounded by a shell of schreibersite, outside of which is a shell of cohenite. The Widmanstätten figures are broad and interrupted, giving the mass an almost granular appearance.
A complete individual; in shape an irregular, elongated, four-sided pyramid.

metbull.alternateNameNote: The official MetBull name search lists Cañon Diablo as a synonym of Canyon Diablo; the Arizona iron and 1891 context agree.

holdings.description: An irregular chiseled piece showing a torn surface.

metbull.alternateNameNote: No official CSV name or MetBull synonym establishes this identity, and the source states that the Siberian locality was absent from its gazetteer.

holdings.description: A polished slab in which the stony portion exceeds the metallic. The iron shows delicate Widmanstätten figures.
A polished piece in which the iron exceeds the stony matter in amount.

metbull.alternateNameNote: MetBull's checker and Steinbach detail page list Rittersgrün as a synonym; the source's Erzgebirge pallasitic-iron context agrees.

holdings.description: A polished slab 126 x 124 x 4 to 6 mm. in size, showing the original surface of the mass on all edges. The Widmanstätten figures are long and slender, with occasional broad bands. Many of the interspaces show a second, much smaller set of markings. One large nodule of troilite.

An irregular piece, one side of which has been polished and etched. The particles of iron show Widmanstätten figures. The outer surface has been much rusted. The olivine and other stony matter exceed the iron in amount, and the whole seems to be identical with the specimens from Rittersgrün, No. 13/2. They are probably parts of the same fall.

metbull.alternateNameNote: MetBull lists Breitenbach as a synonym of Steinbach; the source Erzgebirge stony-iron context agrees.

holdings.description: Twenty-two complete individuals, ranging in weight from 1.5 g. to 26.2 g. All show the nickel-white, rounded knobs of iron.
An irregular mass, apparently showing none of the original crust.
holdings.provenance: (Purchased from Miss F. A. M. Hitchcock.)

holdings.description: An irregular mass like the last, but showing a little of the crust.

About half of a spheroidal mass, in which the iron much predominates over the included olivine. Much of the original surface has scaled off, but many of the pits still show. Apparently different from No. 13/20, and may be the pallasite of Imilac.

metbull.alternateNameNote: MetBull links Desert of Atacama to Copiapo, but Hovey treats the two specimens as different and tentatively suggests Imilac for no. 13/8; the heading alone cannot identify either occurrence.

holdings.description: A very irregular, spongy iron, which has lost its original inclusions, closely resembling the original Pallas iron.

metbull.alternateNameNote: The apparent spelling resembles Ensisheim, but the source locality Elbogen, Bohemia and iron-stone classification conflict with MetBull's French LL6 fall.

holdings.description: A sharp-pointed, irregular mass of very spongy iron, from which the stony matter has largely decomposed and has fallen out to some extent. Apparently different from No. 13/8.

metbull.alternateNameNote: MetBull links Desert of Atacama to Copiapo, but Hovey treats the two specimens as different and tentatively suggests Imilac for no. 13/8; the heading alone cannot identify either occurrence.

holdings.description: An irregular, spongy iron, which has lost its original inclusions.

holdings.description: A sub-rectangular individual with grayish-black skin, which has been removed at one spot showing the gray interior with its minute particles of iron.

A complete, rudely wedge-shaped individual preserving its dull black crust nearly entire. The surface is indented with closely-set small pits. The description makes it probable that this is the correct locality for this stone, though none was given on the Spang label.
A fragment from the interior, preserving none of the crust. This is a gray rock with minute metallic (iron) points scattered thickly through it.
A complete, hemispheroidal individual, preserving its thin rusty-black crust. A chipped place shows the light gray interior with its metallic grains.

A complete, wedge-shaped individual. The comparatively thick, dull-black crust is intersected by a network of fine cracks. The interior is gray with small brown spots in it, and with numerous fine veins and particles of iron scattered through it.
Two smaller complete individuals presenting the same characters.

metbull.alternateNameNote: The source's Transylvania stone fall on 3 February 1882 uniquely agrees with official Mocs; only the historical spelling differs.

holdings.description: A cuboidal fragment from the interior. Light gray rock with numerous small brown patches. Numerous particles of iron are scattered through the mass, and there is one angular piece (part of a crystal ?) of pyrrhotite.

A nearly complete individual, roughly pyramidal in shape, showing broad shallow surface pits. The thin, dull-black crust has been broken off in spots, revealing the dark gray interior with minute metallic points scattered through it. This is the fall entered as “West Liberty” in the British Museum catalogue of meteorites.

holdings.description: Ein Stück von dem ungefähr 270 Pfund schwer gewesenen Meteorsteine. Die Steinart ist von größerer Festigkeit und dichterem Korn, schiefergrau mit weißlich grauen Adern, größtentheils von schiefrigem Gefüge und ohne Körner. Sie zeigt dunkel schiefergraue glänzende Absonderungsflächen sowie metallisch glänzende Partien und Adern aus Gediegeneisen und Schwefeleisen; manche kleineren Teile sind dem Olivin ähnlich. An Chladnis Stück befindet sich keine Rinde.

holdings.description: Ein eckiges Stück mit drei beinahe rechtwinklig zusammentreffenden Seiten, die von einer an den Kanten etwas wulstigen, schwarzen oder schwarzbraunen, etwas glänzenden Rinde mit Adern und Eindrücken bedeckt sind. Der dunkelgraue, ziemlich harte Hauptbestandteil enthält kleine hellere oder weißliche Partien, viele glänzende Teilchen von Gediegeneisen, etwas Eisenoxyd und kleine Kugeln einer schwärzlichen Steinart; Schwefeleisen ist kaum zu bemerken.

holdings.description: Ein Stück ohne Rinde, dessen eine Seite vom Feuer oder Rauch des Meteors stark geschwärzt ist und den Anfang einer Rindenbildung zu zeigen scheint. Das aschgraue Innere enthält viel Gediegeneisen in kleinen und größeren Partien sowie als streifigen Anflug, wenig Eisenoxyd und Schwefeleisen und keine weiteren bemerkten Gemengteile.

holdings.description: Ein Stück mit einer etwas dickeren, graulich oder bräunlich schwarzen, glanzlosen Rinde mit parallelen Streifen. Das sehr weiche Innere ist weißlich oder hellgrau und enthält glimmerartig glänzende Teile, gleichförmig eingemengte feine metallische silberweiß glänzende Punkte, einzelne dunkelgraue oder schwärzliche Körner sowie etwas röthlich anlaufendes Schwefeleisen und Eisenoxyd. Eine Spalte ist, soweit der Brand des Meteors eindringen konnte, schwarzbraun gefärbt.

holdings.description: Ein Stück mit zwei eckigen, von Rinde bedeckten Seiten mit Adern und Eindrücken; an den Kanten bildet die Rinde wulstige Hervorragungen und zeigt zahlreiche Punkte und Körner von Gediegeneisen. Das dunkle, eisenreiche Innere enthält viel Gediegeneisen von unregelmäßiger, teils annähernd tafelförmiger Gestalt. holdings.description: Eine kleine, wohl für die Fassung in einen Ring bestimmte Antike, etwa 3 Linien lang und etwas über 2 Linien breit, unten convex, oben flacher und an einem Ende etwas abgebrochen. The interior, where seen, is light-gray, with coarse metallic particles. In the group is the stone which fell into a haystack without setting it on fire. Cat. Nos., 340-41, 326.

records.name: Locust Grove

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Nearly complete individual, made up of four pieces which have been placed together along the line of original fracture. Together with these is a large number of smaller pieces, varying in weight from 10,000 grammes to 5 grammes, probably also a part of the same individual at the time it fell to the earth. The surface of the main mass is indented by shallow, elliptical pits, the long axes of which run in parallel directions. The crust is smooth and brown, but in many places coated with a white incrustation of carbonate of lime, derived from the soil in which the stone lay. The interior of the mass shows a very compact, fine-grained texture, with few metallic grains; color, dark-green. The smaller fragments are much rusted by exposure. Cat. No., 350.

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Fragment from interior, polished. Made up chiefly of metallic grains, and a dark-brown, chrysolite-like mineral. Cat. No., 280.
Slice, showing crust. Interior portion like previous specimen. Cat. No., 281.

records.name: Tomhannock Creek

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Full-sized, etched section 8 x 12 cm., with crust. Shows typical octahedral figures with small troilite inclusions bordered by kamacite. Cat. No., 477.

records.name: Tonganoxie

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Fragment from interior. Light-gray, with minute metallic grains. Outlines of chondri not discernible. Friable. Cat. No., 486.

records.name: Tourinnes-la-Grosse

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Thin slab, etched, showing typical Widmanstätten figures, the plates of which intersect at angles of 35°. Cat. No., 81.

records.name: Trenton

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Cubical fragment, with crust on two surfaces. The latter shining, black, only slightly pitted, 3 mm. thick. Interior very compact, coarse-grained, the metallic portion forming a network which encloses dark, spherical chondri, some of a diameter of 2 mm. Cat. No., 268.
Smaller fragment, like previous specimen. Cat. No., 325.

records.name: Trenzano

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Etched fragment showing typical stippled appearance of this iron. Cat. No., 59.

records.name: Tucson

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Fragment from interior. Texture compact and firm. Color grayish-brown, mottled with white and gray. There are also angular inclusions of a lighter color. This stone would seem to be an intermediate chondrite, rather than a gray chondrite, as it is usually designated. Cat. No., 543.

records.name: Tysnes

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Cleavage fragments with surface considerably oxidized. Cat. No., 63.

records.name: Union County

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Fragment with crust. Structure fine-granular, with metallic and non metallic minerals about equally distributed. Cat. No., 170.
Similar to No. 170, except that the surface appears glazed and shines in iridescent colors. Cat. No., 171.

records.name: Vaca Muerta (Sierra de Chaco)

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites
records.name: Veramin

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Fragment with crust. Interior gray, compact, flecked with rusty iron grains. Several delicate black veins traverse the specimen. Cat. No., 242.
Thin chip, polished. Well-marked chondri make up the larger part of the mass. Fine metallic grains are numerous. Cat. No., 243.

records.name: Vouillé

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Mass from interior. For the most part light-gray in color, the remaining portion harder and darker. Large chondri are visible in the latter portion. Cat. No., 309.
Fragment with crust. The latter thin, dull-black, blebby. A dark vein passes through a portion of the specimen. Cat. No., 310.
Fragment from interior. Much weathered. Cat. No., 311.

records.name: Waconda

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Fragment from interior. Resembles a piece of hardened, sandy mud or blue clay, with a few metallic grains visible. Cat. No., 317.

records.name: Warrenton

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Segment, 11.5 x 7.5 cm., showing etched and natural surfaces. Widmanstätten figures distinct and regular. Scattered grains of troilite are present. A marked tendency to octahedral cleavage is apparent. Cat. No., 132.

records.name: Welland

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Fragment with crust. The latter thin, dull-black. Interior divided into yellowish and bluish-gray portions distinctly separated in outline and color. The chondri, of which the mass is largely made up, give it the appearance of a fine conglomerate. Cat. No., 224.

records.name: Weston

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Etched section, 18 x 27 cm. Shows coarse Widmanstätten figures, nodules of troilite and scattered flakes of schreibersite. Cat. No., 41.

records.name: Wichita County

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Three polished chips, showing chondri and metallic grains, both coarse and fine. Cat. No., 215.

records.name: Wold Cottage

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Etched fragment, showing typical octahedral figures. Cat. No., 494.

records.name: Wooster

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Fragments from interior. Gray, with dark chondri and rusty iron grains. Cat. No., 259.

records.name: Yatoor

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Full-sized, elongated slab, 10 x 27 cm., showing pittings, crust, polished and etched surface. The Widmanstätten figures are coarse, many of the plates being 1.5-2 cm. in thickness. They are also crossed by a series of finer plates nearly at right angles. Troilite and schreibersite are present. See Plate XXXVII. Cat. No., 118.

records.name: Youndegin

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Thin fragment, etched. No Widmanstätten figures. Cat. No., 28.

records.name: Zacatecas

records.section: Catalogue of the Collection of Meteorites

holdings.description: Fragment from interior of uniform gray color, with minute, shining metallic grains. Texture rather firm. One surface is slickensided and evidences of brecciation are seen in other portions. Cat. No., 548.

holdings.description: Morceau d'un Aérolithe tombé à Losse, département des Landes, en 1790. Suivant les rédacteurs du Bulletin polymathique de Bordeaux (t. 1, p. 39, janvier 1803), en mai 1790, on aperçut dans la commune de Roquefort, département des Landes, vers 10 heures du soir, par un temps très-serein, un corps lumineux qui se dirigeoit du midi au nord. Il éclata à Losse à 2 lieues de Roquefort. On trouva le lendemain, dans une étendue de terrain d'environ une demi-lieue, plusieurs pierres parfaitement semblables et de différentes grosseurs, dont une pesoit environ 80 livres. Dans les endroits où l'on en trouvoit, des ouvertures de forme conique s'étoient faites dans la terre ; leur grandeur et leur profondeur varioient avec le volume de la pierre. M. Darlès, pharmacien à Bordeaux, les a très-bien décrites.
holdings.provenance: Donné en 1802 par MM. Rodrigues et Goethals, directeurs du Muséum d'instruction publique de Bordeaux.

records.name: Losse

metbull.alternateNameNote: The source describes the 1790 Landes fall at Losse near Roquefort; MetBull lists Landes and Roquefort as synonyms of Barbotan.

holdings.description: Fer natif ramuleux, brun, criblé de pores comme une éponge grossière et renfermant des grains d'une matière vitreuse, jaune légèrement nuancé de verdâtre, regardée par quelques-uns comme analogue au péridot, auquel elle ressemble en effet beaucoup. Les deux morceaux proviennent de la masse découverte en 1750 par feu Pallas sur la cime d'une haute montagne, entre l'Oubeï et le Sisim, laquelle renferme une mine de fer compacte. Cette masse, que les Tartares regardent comme étant tombée du ciel, pesoit près de 40 pouds ou 1600 livres russes (environ 700 kilogrammes). On en a détaché différens morceaux, et le reste a été placé dans le cabinet de Saint-Pétersbourg.
holdings.provenance: Du pays de Krasnojarsk, dans la Sibérie méridionale ; provenant de la masse découverte en 1750 par feu Pallas, associé étranger de l'Institut Impérial de France.

a) Den af BERZELIUS undersökta stenen; två små fragmenter. Den bildar en nästan homogen, leucitlik, hvit eller svagt grönaktig, fettglänsande massa, i hvilken endast här och der smärre svarta, efter hvad det tycks oktaödriska prickar äro insprängda. Fragmenterna öfverensstämma fullständigt med BERZELII beskrifning på det mineral han analyseradt och bestå, såsom nämnde analys utvisar, af ungefär 93 % i syror löslig olivin, 6 % olösliga silikater, magnetisk jernmalm, svafveljern och 1 % kromjern.

holdings.description: b) Bit af den i Helsingfors Universitets samling förvarade, af ARPPE beskrifna meteoriten. Beståndsdelarne äro sammanbundne med ett löst, grått bindemedel, hvarigenom det hela får utseende nära nog af groft murbruk, som på vissa ställen är betäckt med en vackert glänsande, svart hinna.

(b) 31 small fragments. Catalogue numbers, (a) 20282; (b) 46,072.

One hundred and nine complete individuals varying in size from that of a pea to that of a hen’s egg; their surfaces show rounded knobs and are partly steel white and partly steel blue to black in color. A section shows the iron in spongiform masses, nodules, and irregular flakes distributed through the stony ground mass. The olivine nodules from above show a vitreous crust with marked lines of flow.
